title: tunna conformance case file
description: One file holds related cases. A case is an ordered list of steps. Each step sends one request and checks the response. Values captured from a response are available to later steps as {{name}} substitutions in path segments, query values, headers and JSON bodies.

decision.description: The ADR or wire.md section this case proves, for example ADR-0004 or wire.md 6.2.

fixtures.description: Names from fixtures.json the runner must provision before this case. Default: all.

capture.description: name → JSON pointer (RFC 6901) into the response body, or 'header:<Name>' for a response header. Captured values substitute {{name}} in later steps. In expect.json a captured number keeps its type where the placeholder is the whole string: "{{name}}" stands for the number.

path.description: Decoded path segments. The runner encodes them. {{name}} substitution applies.

auth.description: How the runner signs the request. 'none' sends no credentials. A key name signs in header form with that fixture key and the runner's clock. A presign object signs in presigned form.

time_offset_seconds.description: Added to the runner's clock to produce the request timestamp. Use to provoke clock_skew.

corrupt_signature.description: Flip a bit in the signature after computing it. Use to provoke bad_signature.

expires_in_seconds.description: Relative to the runner's clock. Negative to provoke presign_expired.

tamper_query.description: Name-value pairs replaced in the URL after it is signed, so the server sees a query the signature does not cover. Use to prove a parameter is bound.

body.description: At most one form. 'json' is serialized by the runner. 'text' is sent as UTF-8. 'bytes' is a deterministic generated body: 'seed' and 'length' produce the same bytes in every runner via the generator defined in fixtures.json. 'hex' is literal bytes.

expect_continue.description: Send Expect: 100-continue. Runners that cannot control this may ignore it.

error.description: Expected error code from errors.json. Implies the error body shape and the status from the table; a case may still state status explicitly.

headers.description: Header name → exact value, or {present: true|false}. Names are case-insensitive.

json.description: Subset match: every field given here must be present in the response body with this value. Objects match by subset, recursively. Arrays must have the same length and each element matches by the same rule, so an array of objects is a subset match per element.

json_present.description: JSON pointers that must resolve in the response body, whatever their value. For fields like server_time whose value the case cannot predict.

json_absent.description: JSON pointers that must not resolve in the response body.

body_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw response body, for binary responses.

body_bytes.description: The body equals the generated bytes for this seed and length. Offsets are the concatenation of parts uploaded with the same seed.
